parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Chlorine trifluoride, $\text{ClF}_3$, decomposes on heating into its elements, as shown.

reaction 1 $$2\text{ClF}_3\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{F}_2\text{(g)}$$

Standard entropies are shown in Table 3.2.

Table 3.2

| substance | $\text{ClF}_3\text{(g)}$ | $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ | $\text{F}_2\text{(g)}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $S^\ominus / \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ | +281.6 | +223.1 | +203.0 |

Calculate the standard entropy change, $\Delta S^\ominus$, in $\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$, for reaction 1.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Group 2 carbonates decompose on heating. The decomposition for one of the Group 2 carbonates, $\text{MCO}_3$, is shown in reaction 2.

reaction 2 $$\text{MCO}_3\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{MO}\text{(s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$

Predict the sign of the entropy change, $\Delta S$, for reaction 2.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The Gibbs equation is shown.

$$\Delta G^\ominus = \Delta H^\ominus - T\Delta S^\ominus$$

Fig. 3.1 shows values of the Gibbs free energy change, $\Delta G^\ominus$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, at different temperatures, $T$, in $\text{K}$, for reaction 2.

Assume $\Delta H^\ominus$ and $\Delta S^\ominus$ values for this reaction remain constant over this temperature range.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 3.1

Use the gradient and intercept on the $y$-axis in Fig. 3.1 and the Gibbs equation to determine:

- $\Delta S^\ominus$, in $\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$, for reaction 2
- the minimum temperature, $T$, in $\text{K}$, at which the reaction is feasible
- $\Delta H^\ominus$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, for reaction 2.
